title: The Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem in its rational unit-cube form: if A is a 0/1 matrix in which every column has at most t ≥ 1 ones and x ∈ [0,1]^N has rational coordinates, then x can be rounded to y ∈ {0,1}^N with |∑ᵢ A j i (y i − x i)| < t for every row j; moreover the rounding can keep every coordinate of x that is already 0 or 1. The proof is the floating-coordinates argument: while some coordinates are strictly between 0 and 1, the rows with more than t floating coordinates are fewer than the floating coordinates, so a nonzero direction keeps their sums fixed, and moving along it makes a coordinate integral; induction on the number of floating coordinates.
